m.chalisa.do1: Remembering Viśvanātha in my mind and fixing my meditation on Gaṇeśa, I compose the Bhairava Chālīsā: Lord, be gracious.
m.chalisa.do2: I worship Baṭukanātha Bhairava, darling son of Śrī Kālī. Be gracious to Chītaramala, O kotwāl (guardian) of Kāśī.
m.chalisa.cau1: Victory, victory to the darling son of Śrī Kālī; be ever merciful to your servant.
m.chalisa.cau2: Bhairava is fearsome, terrible, the bearer of the skull; he is full of wrath, and there is redness in his eyes.
m.chalisa.cau3: In his hand is a hard and dreadful trident; round the Lord's neck is a garland of severed heads.
m.chalisa.cau4: His form and the colour of his body are dark, and he is huge; having drunk wine, he stays intoxicated.
m.chalisa.cau5: You are Rudra and Baṭuka, the companion of your devotees; you are lord of the ghosts, lord of the spirits, and wearer of serpents.
m.chalisa.cau6: Trailateśa is your name; you are Cakratuṇḍa and the beloved Amareśa, lord of the immortals.
m.chalisa.cau7: On his brow the moon shines as a crest; the Lord roars, riding on his dog.
m.chalisa.cau8: Master, you are Śiva, Nakuleśa and Caṇḍa. Lord Baijanātha, salutations; I bow to you.
m.chalisa.cau9: You are hailed as Aśvanātha and Krodheśa; the world has known you as Bhairoṃ and as Kāla.
m.chalisa.cau10: Gāyatrī calls you Nimiṣa and Digambara; you are Jagannātha, of lofty grandeur.
m.chalisa.cau11: You are called Kṣetrapāla, guardian of the land, and Daśapāṇa, the ten-handed; you are called the lovely Umānanda, joy of Umā.
m.chalisa.cau12: You are Cakranātha, who works your devotees' good; all men and women call you Tryambaka.
m.chalisa.cau13: Saṃhāraka and Sunanda are your names: fulfil your devotee's wishes.
m.chalisa.cau14: You are the beloved lord of the piśācas; wipe out all our troubles.
m.chalisa.cau15: O Kṛtyāyu, lovely one, bliss itself: cut the snares of your devotees.
m.chalisa.cau16: You are Kāraṇa and Lamba, the breaker of fear. Salutations, Lord; victory to you, delight of people's hearts.
m.chalisa.cau17: Lord, you are the three-eyed god; your devotees bow their heads at your feet.
m.chalisa.cau18: You are Asitāṅga, Rudra's darling son; you are Mahākāla, the Death even of deaths.
m.chalisa.cau19: You release from torment and destroy the hosts of the enemy; the moon gives its light on your forehead.
m.chalisa.cau20: Your body is white, dark and red; on your brow is a crown, and on your head a turban.
m.chalisa.cau21: Mighty son of Kālī, how far can I tell your splendour?
m.chalisa.cau22: Merciful incarnation of Śiva, having drunk the cup of wine you stay full and merry.
m.chalisa.cau23: You are called the kotwāl of Kāśī. Baṭukanātha, show your wonders.
m.chalisa.cau24: On Sundays people offer you food, and present incense, lamps and naivedya.
m.chalisa.cau25: Seeing you, your devotees are enraptured, and they give you a stream of liquor to drink.
m.chalisa.cau26: In your shrine lovely tassels hang. Bhairoṃ Bābā, bring our undertakings to success.
m.chalisa.cau27: Lord, your fame is not small; a handsome whip graces your hand.
m.chalisa.cau28: Sweet-toned bells ring at your waist; you shine on a throne of gold.
m.chalisa.cau29: All men and women meditate on you and gain the fruit they wish for, all that the heart longs for.
m.chalisa.cau30: The bhopās are your priests; they perform the āratī and great service.
m.chalisa.cau31: Bhairava, I sing of your bhāt (the gifts a brother brings to his sister's family wedding), and again and again bow my head at your feet.
m.chalisa.cau32: You yourself hastened away to Chījana, and Ailādī broke into weeping and wailing.
m.chalisa.cau33: Ailādī said: Where does a brother go, forsaking his sister? Without you, who will give me the bhāt?
m.chalisa.cau34: Baṭukanātha wept in his compassion, and you went off to Hivārā.
m.chalisa.cau35: The girl Ailādī was stricken with grief; then Śiva's throne shook.
m.chalisa.cau36: On the day the time of the wedding came, the Lord sent you at once.
m.chalisa.cau37: Viṣṇu said: Make no delay; go, Bhairava, for three days.
m.chalisa.cau38: Taking a band of Paṭhāns with him, he hastened there and gave Ailādī the bhāt.
m.chalisa.cau39: He fulfilled his sister's hope and laid a red scarf upon her head.
m.chalisa.cau40: Having given the bhāt in full, Bhairava, the treasury of virtues, returned. Salutations, indweller of all hearts; I bow to you.
m.chalisa.do3: Victory, victory, victory to Baṭuka Bhairava, the Master: ward off our troubles. Incarnation of Śiva, be gracious to your servant.
m.chalisa.do4: In the home of whoever reads this Chālīsā a hundred times with love there is every joy, and boundless prosperity grows.
